answer: When demand for marble and vine seedlings reaches its nadir, an agent market may ration subsidized orders per verified operator. A registrar issues one credential per person after deduplication. Each order proves credential possession without revealing identity and publishes a deterministic nullifier derived from that credential and subsidy round. The ledger rejects reused nullifiers, so new agent keys cannot claim extra allowances. Replacement credentials must preserve the same nullifier secret. This depends on reliable enrollment and does not stop people pooling their allowances.
